issues.t: Rear drive motor wiring can short, cutting power (recall)
issues.sym: The truck may suddenly lose drive power while you are driving.
issues.why: Some wires inside the rear electric drive motor did not have enough insulation and can touch each other. GM recall 24V320 covers a small number of 2024 trucks, and the fix is a new rear drive unit.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls on the GMC or NHTSA site. If the recall is open, call a GMC EV dealer to schedule the free drive unit replacement.

issues.t: Service High Voltage or Unable to Charge message
issues.sym: A "Service High Voltage" or "Unable to Charge" message or check engine light appears. DC fast charging may stop working while home (AC) charging still works.
issues.why: GM traced this to several things: a software glitch, snow, ice or moisture in the charge port, plugging in while the truck is not in Park, or, less often, a real high-voltage insulation fault or short in the fast-charge wiring. A GM bulletin covers the 2024 Sierra Denali EV and other GM EVs.
issues.next: Make sure the truck is in Park before plugging in, and check the charge port for ice or debris. If the message stays, book a dealer visit; they will read the codes, test the high-voltage system and load any software update.

issues.t: A/C stops working with a high-voltage battery service message
issues.sym: The air conditioning stops cooling, and a message asks you to service the high-voltage battery system. It has been reported at low mileage.
issues.why: On EVs the A/C compressor runs on high-voltage power and shares a cooling loop with the battery, so a fault in the battery system can shut the A/C off. The exact cause in the reported case was not published.
issues.next: Do not ignore a high-voltage service message. Contact a GMC EV dealer; this should be covered by the new-vehicle warranty.

issues.t: Loss of drive power with the dash screens going dark
issues.sym: While driving, the truck loses propulsion and the speedometer and other displays go black.
issues.why: An owner reported this to NHTSA; the cause was not stated. A power or communication fault in the drive system or electronics can shut down both drive power and screens.
issues.next: If it happens, signal, steer to a safe spot and stop. Have the truck towed to a GMC EV dealer rather than driving it, and file a report with NHTSA.

issues.t: Unexpected braking or brake assist faults when reversing
issues.sym: The truck brakes hard on its own while backing up, even with parking assist turned off, and brake assist fault messages come up. Some owners also feel a strong pull when accelerating.
issues.why: An owner complaint to NHTSA describes repeated brake assist faults and false automatic braking in reverse. Rear sensors that misread obstacles or a brake control software fault can cause it.
issues.next: Note when it happens and any messages shown, then have a dealer check the brake control and parking sensors for faults and updates.

issues.t: Adaptive cruise speeds up after misreading speed limit signs
issues.sym: With adaptive cruise or driver assist on, the truck speeds up toward a much higher limit (for example 75 mph in a 35 mph zone) without the driver asking for it.
issues.why: An owner reported to NHTSA that the system misread speed signs or map data. The cause has not been confirmed by GM.
issues.next: Stay ready to brake whenever cruise or hands-free driving is on, and watch the set speed. Report it to the dealer and to NHTSA.

issues.t: Front turn signals hard to see next to parking lights (recall)
issues.sym: Other drivers may not notice your front turn signals because they look almost as bright as the parking lights.
issues.why: The headlamp LED driver module set the turn signals and parking lights too close in brightness, which fails the federal lighting rule. Recall 24V755 covers about 1,960 2024 Sierra EVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the headlamp LED driver module for free.

issues.t: Rear center seat belt bolt may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no sign at all. A loose belt anchor might feel wobbly, but usually you cannot tell.
issues.why: The bolt that holds the rear middle seat belt to the seat frame may not have been tightened at the factory, so the belt may not hold a passenger in a crash. Recall 25V015 covers a few trucks that were still at dealers.
issues.next: If you bought a 2024 or 2025 Sierra EV, run your VIN through a recall check. The dealer tightens the bolt for free.

issues.t: Stability control warning light may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: If the stability control system has a fault, the warning light may not turn on the next time you start the truck, so you would not know.
issues.why: A software problem in the electronic brake control module keeps the warning from showing. Recall 25V594 covers some 2026 Sierra EVs and Silverado EVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The fix is a free software update at the dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Air suspension fault or sagging from an air leak
issues.sym: An air suspension warning appears, the truck sits lower on one corner, or the compressor runs more than usual.
issues.why: GM bulletins point to a pinched air intake hose for the suspension compressor (code C1197) and to air leaks at the shock valve. GM tells dealers to replace just the air valve when that is the leak, not the whole shock, and to update the ride control software.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the suspension codes. If the truck is clearly leaning or the warning stays on, avoid heavy loads or towing until it is checked.

issues.t: Rear lower control arm bolts may not be tight
issues.sym: You may hear a clunk from the rear, notice the steering pulling, or see uneven tire wear.
issues.why: GM found some rear lower control arm bolts were not fully tightened at the factory. Its fix is to tighten all four bolts and do a rear wheel alignment.
issues.next: Ask a GMC dealer to check whether your VIN is covered by this campaign, and have it done soon because these bolts hold the rear suspension in place.

issues.t: Headlights, turn signals or daytime lights flicker or go out
issues.sym: The headlights, turn signals or daytime running lights flicker or stop working.
issues.why: GM has an open engineering investigation into exterior lighting faults on these trucks and asks dealers to collect details before replacing parts.
issues.next: Check all your lights. If any are out or flickering, avoid night driving until fixed and have the dealer diagnose it.

issues.t: Super Cruise drifts off lane center
issues.sym: With Super Cruise hands-free driving on, the truck does not stay centered in the lane.
issues.why: GM says a software issue causes it and released a software fix.
issues.next: Keep your eyes on the road and be ready to steer. Ask the dealer for the latest software.

issues.t: Front trunk (e-Trunk) stops opening or closing
issues.sym: The power front trunk will not open or close as it should, or stops partway.
issues.why: The e-Trunk can lose its learned open and close positions. A GM software update re-teaches it.
issues.next: Do not force it. Book a dealer visit for the e-Trunk update.

issues.t: Rattles or squeaks from the dash or headliner
issues.sym: Buzzing or rattling from the right side of the dash near the windshield, or squeaks from the headliner over bumps.
issues.why: Trim pieces touch or move against each other. GM has repair steps for both the dash and the headliner.
issues.next: Note where and when the noise happens and ask the dealer to apply the GM noise repairs under warranty.

issues.t: Alarm goes off for no reason
issues.sym: The theft alarm sounds when no one is near the truck.
issues.why: GM traced it to a software glitch in the body control module.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the GM fix for unwanted alarms.

issues.t: Trailer tire pressures show wrong
issues.sym: When towing, the trailer tire pressure readings on the screen are wrong.
issues.why: GM says a software issue causes the wrong readings.
issues.next: Check trailer tires with a gauge before each trip until the dealer updates the software.

issues.t: Radio or head-up display not working right
issues.sym: The radio or infotainment acts up, or the head-up display does not show on the windshield.
issues.why: GM has a bulletin to reprogram the radio module for a software problem, and owners have reported the head-up display not showing.
issues.next: Try restarting the truck. If it keeps happening, ask the dealer for the radio software update.

issues.t: Soft tonneau cover comes loose at highway speed
issues.sym: The bed cover comes loose at the front and flaps loudly at highway speed, or lifts off near the cab.
issues.why: Owners report the cover's front anchor points let go. A loose cover can fly off and hit other cars.
issues.next: Pull over safely and secure or remove the cover. Have the dealer inspect the mounts before using it again.

issues.t: Truck rolls after the parking brake is set
issues.sym: After setting the parking brake on a slope, the truck still rolls.
issues.why: An owner reported this to NHTSA; the cause has not been confirmed.
issues.next: Always shift to Park and turn the wheels toward the curb on hills. Have the dealer test the parking brake right away.

issues.t: Bumping noise from the front suspension
issues.sym: A bump or knock from the front passenger side when driving over rough pavement.
issues.why: An owner reported this to NHTSA; the source was not found. Loose or worn suspension parts can cause it.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the front suspension under warranty.
